```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

van den Brink et al. (2019) measured 76 biogenic amines and amino acids in rat
plasma and in striatal brain extracellular fluid (brain ECF, by microdialysis)
after intravenous quinpirole, a dopamine D2/3 agonist, and summarised the
responses with a *cluster-based* PK/PD model: biomarkers whose time courses
look alike are grouped by k-means clustering and each cluster gets one PK/PD
model. The authors fitted two separate NONMEM models -- one for the plasma
clusters (driven by plasma quinpirole) and one for the brain ECF clusters
(driven by brain ECF quinpirole) -- and both are packaged here:

```{r models}
mod_pl <- readModelDb("vandenBrink_2019_quinpirole_rat_plasma")
mod_br <- readModelDb("vandenBrink_2019_quinpirole_rat_brain")
```

* Plasma model: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_pl)$description`
* Brain model: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_br)$description`
* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_pl)$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12370> (open access; the NONMEM
  control streams are Data S1, brain, and Data S2, plasma)
* Quinpirole PK model: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bph.14452> (van den Brink 2018,
  Table 1 and Supporting Information Equation S3)

# Population

Forty-four male Wistar rats with femoral artery and vein cannulas and
microdialysis probes in both caudate putamina (striatum) received 0
(n = 12), 0.17 (n = 16) or 0.86 (n = 16) mg/kg quinpirole intravenously on
experiment day 1 and again on day 8, with the same dose given subcutaneously
every day in between. Plasma was sampled at -5, 5, 7.5, 10, 15, 25, 45, 90, 120
and 180 min and microdialysate in 20-min fractions. Body weight was not
reported. The quinpirole PK model was developed in the parent study on
0.17-2.14 mg/kg IV data from the same animals. Eight-day dosing did not change
basal biomarker levels in a way the PK/PD models retained (Results), so the
packaged models carry no experiment-day covariate.

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(mod_pl)$population)
```

## Cluster membership and per-biomarker baselines

Every cluster output is the biomarker level *relative to its typical pre-dose
baseline*. The authors' code scales each cluster by a metabolite-specific
baseline `BSL0 = exp(THETA(m) + ETA(1))`; because every cluster model is linear
in its baseline, the absolute level of metabolite *m* is `exp(THETA(m))` times
the output of its cluster. The cluster of each biomarker is read from the
symbols of Figure 1 (grey symbols are biomarkers whose cluster model was not
significant) and the counts agree with the facet labels of Figure 3. Units
follow the platform: platform A (BrainsOnline, `[BO]`) reports nM, or uM for
glutamate and glycine; platform B reports internal-standard response ratios.


Brain cluster 1 (N6,N6,N6-trimethyllysine) showed no dose response; the
authors excluded it from Table 3 and the brain model carries no cluster 1.

# Virtual cohort and simulation

Each arm gets 100 virtual rats (the study had 12-16). Body weight was not
reported, so every rat is assumed to weigh 0.25 kg; the dose in ug is
`mg/kg x 0.25 x 1000`, given as an IV bolus into `central` at time 0. The
observation rows sit on `central` with `dvid = 1`, which returns every endpoint
column of these multi-endpoint models.

```{r cohort}
wt_kg <- 0.25
arms <- c("0 mg/kg" = 0, "0.17 mg/kg" = 0.17, "0.86 mg/kg" = 0.86)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 180, by = 5), 7.5)))

make_arm <- function(n, dose_mgkg, label, id_offset = 0L, times = obs_times) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose <- tibble(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = dose_mgkg * wt_kg * 1000, evid = 1L,
    cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(treatment = label) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

n_per_arm <- 100L
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(arms), function(i) {
  make_arm(n_per_arm, arms[[i]], names(arms)[i], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

# One rat per arm for the typical-value solves
events_typ <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(arms), function(i) {
  make_arm(1L, arms[[i]], names(arms)[i], id_offset = i - 1L)
}))
```

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190225)
sim_pl <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pl, events, keep = "treatment", useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_br <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_br, events, keep = "treatment", useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Typical-value solves: omega = NA and sigma = NA drop the random effects
typ_pl <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pl, events_typ,
  keep = "treatment", omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE
) |> as.data.frame()
typ_br <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_br, events_typ,
  keep = "treatment", omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE
) |> as.data.frame()
```

# Quinpirole PK (Figure S2)

Figure S2 of the paper (reproduced from van den Brink 2018) is a visual
predictive check of unbound quinpirole in plasma and brain ECF. With a 0.25 kg
rat the typical plasma concentration is about 34 and 170 ng/mL at 5 min after
0.17 and 0.86 mg/kg, and brain ECF concentrations run about five-fold above
plasma once distribution is complete, as the figure shows.

```{r figure-s2}
sim_pl |>
  filter(treatment != "0 mg/kg", time >= 5) |>
  select(id, time, treatment, Plasma = Cc, BrainECF = Cbrain_striatum) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Plasma, BrainECF), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(treatment, matrix, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), Q50 = median(conc), Q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~matrix) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Unbound quinpirole (ng/mL)",
    title = "Quinpirole in plasma and brain ECF (median, 90% interval)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure S2 of van den Brink 2019 (0.17 and 0.86 mg/kg arms)."
  )
```

# Concentration-effect relations (Figure 2)

Figure 2 plots each cluster's drug-effect function `E(C)` against the
concentration at its target site (for the two transit clusters the delay term
is left out, as in the figure). The brain panel of the figure numbers the six
responding clusters 1-6; they are Table 3's brain clusters 2-7.

```{r figure-2}
p_pl <- rxode2::rxode(mod_pl)$theta
p_br <- rxode2::rxode(mod_br)$theta
conc <- 10^seq(-6, 6, length.out = 241)
emax_fun <- function(e, ec50) 1 + e * conc / (ec50 + conc)
imax_fun <- function(i, ic50) 1 - i * conc / (ic50 + conc)
curves <- bind_rows(
  tibble(site = "Plasma", cluster = "1", conc = conc, eff = emax_fun(exp(p_pl[["lemax_c1"]]), exp(p_pl[["lec50_c1"]]))),
  tibble(site = "Plasma", cluster = "2", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_pl[["limax_c23"]]), exp(p_pl[["lec50_c24"]]))),
  tibble(site = "Plasma", cluster = "3", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_pl[["limax_c23"]]), exp(p_pl[["lec50_c37"]]))),
  tibble(site = "Plasma", cluster = "4", conc = conc, eff = emax_fun(exp(p_pl[["lemax_c4"]]), exp(p_pl[["lec50_c24"]]))),
  tibble(site = "Plasma", cluster = "5", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_pl[["limax_c5"]]), exp(p_pl[["lec50_c5"]]))),
  tibble(site = "Plasma", cluster = "6", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_pl[["limax_c6"]]), exp(p_pl[["lec50_c6"]]))),
  tibble(site = "Plasma", cluster = "7", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_pl[["limax_c7"]]), exp(p_pl[["lec50_c37"]]))),
  tibble(site = "BrainECF", cluster = "2", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_br[["limax_c2"]]), exp(p_br[["lec50_c234"]]))),
  tibble(site = "BrainECF", cluster = "3", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_br[["limax_c3"]]), exp(p_br[["lec50_c234"]]))),
  tibble(site = "BrainECF", cluster = "4", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_br[["limax_c4"]]), exp(p_br[["lec50_c234"]]))),
  tibble(site = "BrainECF", cluster = "5", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_br[["limax_c5"]]), exp(p_br[["lec50_c567"]]))),
  tibble(site = "BrainECF", cluster = "6", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_br[["limax_c6"]]), exp(p_br[["lec50_c567"]]))),
  tibble(site = "BrainECF", cluster = "7", conc = conc, eff = imax_fun(exp(p_br[["limax_c7"]]), exp(p_br[["lec50_c567"]])))
)
ggplot(curves, aes(conc, eff, colour = cluster)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~site, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Quinpirole concentration at the target site (nM)", y = "Effect",
    colour = "Table 3 cluster",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of van den Brink 2019."
  )

# Plateaus of Figure 2: 1 + Emax or 1 - Imax at high concentration
plateau <- curves |> filter(conc == max(conc)) |> select(site, cluster, eff)
stopifnot(
  abs(plateau$eff[plateau$site == "Plasma" & plateau$cluster == "1"] - 47.5) < 0.1,
  abs(plateau$eff[plateau$site == "BrainECF" & plateau$cluster == "6"] - 0.33) < 0.01
)
```

# Cluster responses (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows the geometric-mean cluster responses as change from baseline
with the model predictions as dark lines. The typical-value predictions below
are the packaged models' counterpart; the ribbons are the 5th-95th percentiles
of the simulated rats, which include the between-rat baseline variability and
the residual error.

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 8}
cluster_long <- function(sim, site) {
  sim |>
    select(id, time, treatment, starts_with("resp_c")) |>
    pivot_longer(starts_with("resp_c"), names_to = "cluster", values_to = "rel") |>
    mutate(site = site, cluster = sub("resp_c", "Cluster ", cluster))
}
vpc <- bind_rows(cluster_long(sim_pl, "Plasma"), cluster_long(sim_br, "BrainECF")) |>
  group_by(site, cluster, treatment, time) |>
  summarise(Q05 = quantile(rel, 0.05), Q95 = quantile(rel, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
typ <- bind_rows(cluster_long(typ_pl, "Plasma"), cluster_long(typ_br, "BrainECF"))

for (s in c("BrainECF", "Plasma")) {
  print(
    ggplot(filter(typ, site == s), aes(time, rel, colour = treatment)) +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = filter(vpc, site == s),
        aes(x = time, ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95, fill = treatment),
        inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.12
      ) +
      geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
      facet_wrap(~cluster, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = c("red", "darkgreen", "blue")) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "darkgreen", "blue")) +
      labs(
        x = "Time (min)", y = "Change from baseline (ratio)",
        title = s,
        caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of van den Brink 2019 (lines: typical value)."
      )
  )
}
```

The typical-value curves were compared with the prediction lines of Figure 3,
read by the maintainers at the times below (to about +/- 0.05).

```{r figure-3-compare}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~site, ~cluster, ~treatment, ~time, ~figure,
  "BrainECF", "Cluster 3", "0.86 mg/kg", 180, 0.71,
  "BrainECF", "Cluster 5", "0.86 mg/kg", 180, 0.65,
  "BrainECF", "Cluster 6", "0.17 mg/kg", 30, 0.47,
  "BrainECF", "Cluster 6", "0.86 mg/kg", 180, 0.40,
  "BrainECF", "Cluster 7", "0.17 mg/kg", 180, 0.63,
  "BrainECF", "Cluster 7", "0.86 mg/kg", 180, 0.46,
  "Plasma", "Cluster 1", "0.17 mg/kg", 180, 1.60,
  "Plasma", "Cluster 1", "0.86 mg/kg", 180, 3.30,
  "Plasma", "Cluster 2", "0.86 mg/kg", 180, 0.87,
  "Plasma", "Cluster 3", "0.86 mg/kg", 180, 0.85,
  "Plasma", "Cluster 4", "0.86 mg/kg", 180, 1.50,
  "Plasma", "Cluster 5", "0.86 mg/kg", 25, 0.82,
  "Plasma", "Cluster 6", "0.86 mg/kg", 10, 0.62,
  "Plasma", "Cluster 7", "0.86 mg/kg", 180, 0.63
)
cmp3 <- fig3 |>
  left_join(typ |> select(site, cluster, treatment, time, model = rel),
    by = c("site", "cluster", "treatment", "time")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model - figure) / figure)
cmp3 |>
  mutate(model = signif(model, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    "Site" = site, "Cluster" = cluster, "Arm" = treatment, "Time (min)" = time,
    "Figure 3" = figure, "Model" = model, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value cluster responses against Figure 3.")

# Plasma cluster 1 is a known deviation (see Assumptions);
# every other point is within the reading precision of the figure plus the
# PK uncertainty from the unreported body weight.
chk3 <- filter(cmp3, !(site == "Plasma" & cluster == "Cluster 1"))
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(chk3$model),
  abs(median(chk3$pct_diff)) < 5,
  max(abs(chk3$pct_diff)) < 12
)
```

# Model checks

These checks use the typical-value solves, where both sides of each comparison
come from the same parameters, so the bounds are tight.

```{r checks}
# 1. Placebo: no drug, every cluster stays at its baseline of 1.
pl0 <- typ |> filter(treatment == "0 mg/kg")
stopifnot(max(abs(pl0$rel - 1)) < 1e-6)

# 2. Brain clusters 2-4 have IC50 = 0.001 nM, so any dose saturates them and
#    they settle at 1 - Imax (Table 3: 0.80, 0.71, 0.85) for both doses.
sat <- typ |>
  filter(site == "BrainECF", cluster %in% c("Cluster 2", "Cluster 3", "Cluster 4"),
         treatment != "0 mg/kg", time == 180) |>
  mutate(target = c("Cluster 2" = 0.80, "Cluster 3" = 0.71, "Cluster 4" = 0.85)[cluster])
stopifnot(max(abs(sat$rel - sat$target)) < 1e-3)

# 3. Plasma cluster 6 (serotonin, pool model): the pool refills while release
#    is inhibited, so the response returns to baseline within the experiment.
c6 <- typ |> filter(site == "Plasma", cluster == "Cluster 6", treatment == "0.86 mg/kg")
stopifnot(min(c6$rel) < 0.7, abs(c6$rel[c6$time == 180] - 1) < 0.01)

# 4. Unbound brain-to-plasma partitioning: for this linear PK model the ratio
#    of brain ECF to plasma AUC is CL_PL,ECF / CL_ECF,PL = 2.5 / 0.52 (the
#    Kp,uu of about 5 in van den Brink 2018 Table 1).
long_ev <- make_arm(1L, 0.86, "0.86 mg/kg", times = seq(0, 3000, by = 5))
long <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pl, long_ev,
  omega = NA, sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE, keep = "treatment"
) |> as.data.frame()
# rxSolve drops the id column for a single-subject solve
if (!"id" %in% names(long)) long$id <- 1L
auc_tz <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
kpuu <- auc_tz(long$time, long$Cbrain_striatum) / auc_tz(long$time, long$Cc)
stopifnot(abs(kpuu / (2.5 / 0.52) - 1) < 0.01)
kpuu
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA, so PKNCA is used to summarise the simulated
quinpirole exposure per arm and to check the terminal half-life against the
closed form of the two-compartment model (smallest eigenvalue of the rate
matrix), computed from the same typical parameters.

```{r pknca}
# Placebo rats have no quinpirole, so they are left out of the NCA
sim_active <- subset(sim_pl, treatment != "0 mg/kg")
sim_nca <- sim_active |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- subset(events, evid == 1 & treatment != "0 mg/kg") |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 180, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  rename("Arm" = treatment, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "AUC0-180 (min*ng/mL)" = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated plasma quinpirole exposure (median over rats).")

# Terminal half-life on the long typical profile
long_nca <- long |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
hl <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(long_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(filter(long_ev, evid == 1), amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, half.life = TRUE)
))
hl_pknca <- as.data.frame(hl) |> filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |> pull(PPORRES)

k10 <- 0.71 / 60 / 1.0
k12 <- 2.5 / 60 / 1.0
k21 <- 0.52 / 60 / 0.12
rate_mat <- matrix(c(-(k10 + k12), k12, k21, -k21), 2)
hl_closed <- log(2) / min(abs(eigen(rate_mat)$values))
stopifnot(abs(hl_pknca / hl_closed - 1) < 0.02)
c(pknca = hl_pknca, closed_form = hl_closed)
```

The terminal half-life of about `r round(hl_closed)` min (about
`r round(hl_closed / 60, 1)` h) agrees with the decline of the Figure S2
plasma profiles between 25 and 180 min.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Normalised cluster outputs.** The authors fitted each biomarker's own
  level, `BSL0_m x exp(ETA) x R_c(t)`, on the log scale. Because every cluster
  model is linear in the baseline, the packaged models output `R_c(t)` scaled
  by the individual baseline factor `exp(etalrbase)` (typical baseline fixed
  at 1); the per-biomarker baselines `exp(THETA(m))` from the authors' code are
  listed in the table above so absolute levels can be recovered. The code uses
  one `ETA(1)` for every metabolite and cluster, and the packaged models do the
  same.
- **Table 3 against the published plasma code.** The brain control stream
  (Data S1) reproduces Table 3 exactly. The plasma control stream (Data S2)
  carries estimates close to, but not the same as, Table 3: for example plasma
  cluster 4 has Emax 405% against 363%, ktr 0.0044 against 0.0052 1/min and
  kout 0.17 against 9.58 1/min, and the cluster 3 / 7 IC50 is 22 against
  17.2 nM. Table 3 values (the final estimates) are used. Data S2 also shares
  Imax between clusters 5 and 7 and kout between clusters 3 and 5, whereas
  Table 3 reports these pairs with different standard errors (14.6% / 6.4%,
  12.2% / 12.5%), so the packaged plasma model keeps them as separate
  parameters with the Table 3 values (each pair has the same value).
- **Residual error and IIV from the control streams.** Table 3 reports no
  variability; `etalrbase` and the residual SDs come from the `$OMEGA` and
  `$SIGMA` blocks of Data S1 / S2, read as variances. The plasma stream has a
  single `$SIGMA` for all clusters, so its value is repeated on each plasma
  output (nlmixr2 needs one residual parameter per endpoint). For the plasma
  model, whose `$THETA` values differ from Table 3, these variances are those
  of the published control stream.
- **IC50 of 0.001 nM.** Table 3 reports the high-potency IC50 of brain clusters
  2-4 and plasma cluster 6 as 0.001 nM, fixed; the control streams carry
  smaller values (about 2.5e-6 and 1.4e-4 nM). Both make the effect maximal at
  any quinpirole concentration; the Table 3 value is used.
- **Quinpirole PK from the parent study.** The cluster models took individual
  PK parameters from the parent study's fit (data items `CLPOP` ... `VECFPOP`).
  The packaged models carry the population PK model of van den Brink 2018
  (Table 1, Equation S3) instead, with its IIV on clearance and its residual
  errors (read as variances). The bootstrap column of that table prints V_ECF
  as 0.013 L against the 0.12 L estimate; the estimate is used.
- **Body weight and dose administration.** Neither paper reports body weight
  or the duration of the IV dose. The vignette assumes 0.25 kg and an IV bolus;
  with these, the typical plasma and brain ECF concentrations fall within the
  Figure S2 prediction intervals. The models themselves take the dose in ug and
  do not depend on body weight.
- **Plasma cluster 1.** At 180 min the typical value is about 2.6 against
  about 3.3 in Figure 3 after 0.86 mg/kg, and about 1.4 against 1.6 after
  0.17 mg/kg. This cluster rises late (its transit
  delay peaks at ntr / ktr, about 190 min), so it is the most sensitive to
  late quinpirole concentrations, which here depend on the assumed body
  weight and on typical instead of individual PK. It is reported, not
  tuned, and is excluded from the Figure 3 gate.
- **Time after dose.** The transit term uses time after the experiment-day
  dose (`TIM` in Data S2); the models use `tad(central)`, which equals it for
  one IV dose per experiment day.
- **Baseline drift data item.** The control streams multiply the baseline by
  `(1 + BSLP)`, a data item that the paper does not describe; it is taken as 0.
- **Molecular weight.** Table 3 reports potencies in nM while the control
  streams work in ug/L. The conversion uses the free-base molecular weight of
  quinpirole, 219.33 g/mol, which the code-to-table pair for the brain
  cluster 5-7 IC50 (26.8 ug/L, 122 nM) confirms.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for either paper (checked
  2026-11-25).
